problem: Action-centric VLM/VLA navigation policies do not model how observations evolve under predicted motion, and existing world-action models (WAMs) for continuous VLN do not condition joint future-view and action generation on geometry-aware representations inferred from the observed RGB history.
motivation: In continuous navigation every action changes the viewpoint, so the predicted trajectory and its visual transition should be consistent, especially under large viewpoint changes. A monocular history contains multiple views of the same scene, so geometry recovered from it could serve as persistent shared context for future-view and action generation.
key_idea: Feed a frozen VGGT-Omega feature stream through a trainable 3D Scene-to-Token Adapter into a fixed-length clean prefix of a joint video-action DiT (DreamZero-style, Wan2.2-TI2V-5B) so geometry-aware scene tokens condition both future-view and action generation, trained by A* SFT, DAgger-SFT and Counterfactual DanceGRPO.
insight: Replacing the native VAE RGB-history prefix with geometry-derived tokens, with everything else identical (WNM-2D vs WNM-3D), gives +13.1 SR / +8.0 SPL on Seen and +7.6 SR / +3.8 SPL on Unseen, so the geometry conditioning is the source of the gain. In the training-stage ablation, DAgger-SFT gives the largest SR gain (Seen 56.7→80.7) but lengthens paths, and DanceGRPO then cuts trajectory length and raises SPL (Unseen SPL 38.2→46.6). Applying DanceGRPO directly after Stage-I lowers SR (56.7→47.1), so supervised correction on policy-visited states is a prerequisite for reward-guided refinement, though the authors only hypothesize the mechanism.
method: Frozen geometry encoder: VGGT-Omega processes K=33 uniformly sampled monocular RGB history frames (resized to 512x512) and yields multi-level patch features from encoder blocks 5, 12, 18 and 24.
Multi-level fusion: each level is normalized and projected to width 512, then a lightweight gating network softmax-weights levels per lattice location to form a fused source memory of shape 33x32x32.

3D query resampling: the source memory is adaptively pooled to a 9x5x10 target lattice, and learned slot plus structured embeddings (global, temporal, row, column, Fourier coordinates, query type) are added; 2 anchored deformable resampling layers (8 heads x 8 points) with predicted offsets and weights retrieve fine-grained source features.

Spatial-temporal refinement: 2 factorized blocks apply spatial then temporal self-attention plus an MLP, and a detail head plus a coarse residual head on the pooled base output 450 tokens of width d=3072 (23.97M trainable adapter params) as the clean prefix.

Joint world-action DiT: the prefix conditions block-causal attention over B=4 blocks (8 future video frames and 8 actions each), trained with joint flow matching on video latents and actions (dx, dy, dyaw). Only the first action chunk is executed, in receding horizon; predicted frames are never decoded or fed back.

Three-stage training: (I) SFT on 16K A* demonstrations for 20 epochs; (II) DAgger-SFT on policy-visited states (633K chunks for 3D, 691K for 2D) for 5 epochs; (III) Counterfactual DanceGRPO, which samples one intervention transition from each of 4 denoising strata, generates 4 branches with branch-specific noise, and applies group-normalized advantages with modality-routed clipped surrogates.

Stage-III rewards: a visual reward (pyramid SSIM, Charbonnier, temporal terms, degradation factor, optical-flow/action consistency), a navigation reward (geodesic progress, path length, collision, route adherence, yaw) and a stopping reward, computed on ~96K fixed records without stepping the simulator.

setting.backbone: Wan2.2-TI2V-5B world-action DiT (DreamZero-style joint video-action flow) + frozen VGGT-Omega + trainable 3D Scene-to-Token Adapter
setting.training_data: 16K A*-generated demonstrations on GN-Bench tasks (Stage-I), ~633K DAgger chunks (Stage-II), ~96K policy-generated records for DanceGRPO (Stage-III)
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB only (33-frame history sampled from the trajectory plus the current frame; no depth, pose, BEV or map)
setting.action_space: continuous local planar increments (dx, dy, dyaw), 4 chunks of 8 actions; first chunk executed, STOP inferred from small displacement
setting.simulator: GN-Bench (3D Gaussian Splatting environments, GN-0 / GN-Matrix)
setting.privileged: none at test time (A* expert, occupancy maps and GT trajectories are used only in training and reward computation)

numbers.extra: Full 3-stage curriculum (A* SFT + DAgger-SFT + Counterfactual DanceGRPO); official GN-Bench Seen split (1,000 episodes)
numbers.evidence: Table 1 (Evaluation Metrics on GN-Bench), Seen: WNM-3D 10.6 / 1.9 / 94.2 / 88.7 / 80.9

numbers_note: GN-Bench is not in the canonical benchmark list, so it is entered as other:GN-Bench. Its 'Seen' and 'Unseen' splits are mapped to val-seen and test-unseen (an assumption). The stage-ablation rows (Stage-I / Stage-II / direct GRPO) are in Table 2 but omitted here as intermediate variants.
results: WNM-3D reaches 88.7 SR / 80.9 SPL on GN-Bench Seen and 53.5 SR / 46.6 SPL on Unseen. This beats the strongest prior method, GN-BAE with BEV (58.6 SR / 58.6 SPL on Seen), and the strongest FPV-only prior on Unseen (GN-BAE, 38.9 SR / 37.3 SPL). It also beats its 2D-conditioned counterpart WNM-2D (75.6 / 72.9 Seen; 45.9 / 42.8 Unseen).
limitations: Large Seen-to-Unseen gap remains (88.7 vs 53.5 SR); the geometry conditioning does not reduce it, and gains are larger on Seen.
Evaluated only on the GN-Bench simulator (3DGS) with a single seed and no confidence intervals; no real-robot experiments; trajectories are longer than the 2D variant and baselines (TL 10.6 vs 7.9).
Heavy three-stage pipeline (A* expert, DAgger rollouts, DanceGRPO with hand-tuned rewards); the explanation for why DAgger is needed before GRPO is a hypothesis, not verified.
